result.title: Large Language Models for AI Infrastructure
result.summary: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to design, optimize, and operate the infrastructure behind AI training and serving, yet the literature remains fragmented across hardware design, machine learning systems, electronic design automation, and high-performance computing. We present a comprehensive survey of LLM-assisted AI infrastructure across its lifecycle, from accelerator design and kernel engineering to compilation, deployment, operations, data management, and energy optimization. We organize the literature by the primary resource the LLM manages: artifact-centric methods for computational artifacts, operational-centric methods for deployment context and system state, and resource-centric methods for data and energy. These categories span the lifecycle and cover AI-specific concerns such as distributed-training configuration, inference serving, GPU-cluster scheduling, and data loading. Building on this taxonomy, we conduct a cross-study quantitative synthesis of reported results. Because studies adopt heterogeneous benchmarks, baselines, hardware, and metrics, we compare methods only where evaluation conditions permit and align results along common dimensions: functional correctness, execution performance, throughput, resource and energy consumption, operational outcomes, and optimization cost, keeping each result's native metric, baseline, and setting rather than collapsing them into a single score. This comparison reveals where LLM-driven methods yield consistent gains, how reported gains in workload orchestration depend on the evaluation environment, from simulators to real clusters and production, and where evidence is still lacking. Together, the taxonomy, lifecycle perspective, and quantitative evaluation provide an evidence-grounded reference for LLM-driven engineering of AI infrastructure.

AI.brief_summary: 该文是一篇综述，按“产物中心、运维中心、资源中心”三类资源组织 LLM 辅助 AI 基础设施的工作，涵盖加速器设计、kernel、编译、部署与能耗优化，并做跨研究的定量结果对齐。
AI.relevance_reason: 主题为 LLM 参与 AI 系统与硬件工程的综述，其中的“system state”指集群部署与运维上下文，与 VLM 推理中的内部推理状态、视觉证据使用无实质联系，也未提供可核查的 latent reasoning 借鉴线索，故排除。
